does: Cooks food with the dry, even heat of an oven.

intro.what: Baking uses the dry heat of an oven to cook food.
intro.why: It teaches you to watch how food colours and to notice uneven oven heat.

how: Heat the oven fully before the food goes in.
Set the dish on the middle shelf, with space around it for the air to move.
Leave the door shut for the first part of the cooking.
Turn the dish if the oven browns one side faster, and check before the time is up.

cues.text: An even colour across the top, with the edges just darker than the middle.
A toasty smell that reaches the next room is the sign to check.

mistakes.mistake: Putting food into an oven that is still heating, so that it dries out before it colours.
mistakes.fix: Wait until the oven has reached its heat.
Ovens run hot or cold. Learn yours, and judge by colour and feel as well as by time.

quiz.question: What provides the heat when you bake?
choices: Steam trapped in a covered pot.
quiz.because: Baking surrounds food with the dry heat of an oven.

quiz.question: How should you prepare the oven before baking?
choices: Put the food in while the oven warms.
Put the dish near the door so you can check it often.
Heat the oven fully before adding the food.
quiz.because: Heat the oven fully first, so the food does not sit in it throughout the warm-up.

quiz.question: What would suggest that the oven is browning unevenly?
choices: The dish colours more on one side.
The edges colour slightly more than the middle.
quiz.because: More colour on one side shows uneven browning. Turn the dish if that side is browning faster.

quiz.question: The oven dial and the colour of the food seem to disagree. What should guide your next check?
choices: Colour and feel as well as time.
quiz.because: Ovens can run hotter or cooler than their dials suggest. Check the food as well as the time.
